title: Goldset Stewardship + Drift Watchdog for Embeddings and Rerank
creator: Maya Kapoor
description: Build a resilient, production-ready evaluation harness that treats curated goldsets as first-class observability assets and provides continuous drift detection for embedding and rerank endpoints. The harness will: (1) maintain curated goldsets with provenance and versioning; (2) run nightly, windowed scoring across active model variants; (3) produce per-metric baselines (7d, 30d, EWMA) and z-scores; (4) generate prioritized alerts and runbook links for oncall; and (5) surface sample failure cases in the Console for faster debugging. This is targeted at preventing silent regressions during model rollouts and catching production drift impacting customer-facing rerank latency/quality.
acceptance_criteria: Nightly job executes for all goldsets and writes structured metrics to telemetry (count, mean similarity, recall@k, MRR, cosine-shift distribution, latency-percentiles).
Baseline windows (7d, 30d) and EWMA are computed and z-scores are available for each metric and model variant.
Grafana/Kibana alerting rules created for: sustained MRR drop (>1%), median cosine-shift (>0.05), and increased tail latency (>95th percentile), with severity mapping and PagerDuty integration.
CI gate for model promotion checks goldset MRR and cosine-shift; promotion is blocked if MRR drops >1.5% or cosine-shift exceeds configured thresholds.
Console shows per-model and per-customer drift panels with example sentinel queries and links to the golden input and expected output artifacts.

notes: Goldset stewardship: prefer smaller, high-quality curated sets (100-2k rows) grouped by workload; tag rows with 'sentinel' boolean for high-priority examples.

Metric choices: MRR + recall@k for ranking quality, cosine-shift and centroid displacement for embedding drift, and latency p95/p99 for perf regressions; track effect sizes rather than absolute deltas when low variance.
Alert design: multi-stage alerts (warning -> critical) using z-score thresholds and sustained windows (e.g., 3 consecutive nights) to reduce noise.
Sampling/cost: nightly runner will sample shards for very large goldsets to control compute; deterministic sampling seed to keep comparisons stable.
Model variants: evaluate paired comparisons between candidate, baseline, and a lightweight fallback variant to measure regression severity and fallback viability.
Data retention: store nightly scoring artifacts for 90 days and summary baselines for 365 days to support audits and regressions investigations.
